routes.label: Count the integer indices of the sine zeros

question: The number of \(x\)-intercepts on the graph of \(y = \sin(\frac{1}{x})\) in the interval \((0.0001, 0.001)\) is closest to
solution:
An \(x\)-intercept occurs exactly when \(\sin(1/x)=0\). Sine is the vertical coordinate on the unit circle, so its zeros occur precisely at integer multiples of \(\pi\). Since the given \(x\)-values are positive, the intercepts have the form
\[
x=\frac1{k\pi},\qquad k\text{ a positive integer}.
\]
Taking reciprocals reverses the positive endpoint inequalities:
\[
0.0001<x<0.001
\iff 1000<\frac1x<10000.
\]
At a zero, this becomes
\[
\frac{1000}{\pi}<k<\frac{10000}{\pi}.
\]
Using \(3.1415<\pi<3.1416\), the lower bound lies strictly between \(318\) and \(319\), and the upper bound lies strictly between \(3183\) and \(3184\). Therefore the allowed integers are exactly
\[
k=319,320,\ldots,3183.
\]
Every such integer gives one intercept in the open interval, and distinct integers give distinct intercepts. Their number is
\[
3183-319+1=2865.
\]
This is \(35\) away from \(2900\) and \(135\) away from \(3000\); all other choices are still farther away. Thus the answer is \(\boxed{2900}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
